paragraphs: Pinnacle West is an investor-owned electric utility holding company based in Phoenix, Arizona

with consolidated assets of approximately $30 billion. We derive essentially all of our revenues and earnings from our principal subsidiary, APS. Since 1886, APS and its affiliates have provided energy and energy-related products to people and businesses throughout Arizona. APS is Arizona's largest and longest-serving electric company and generates safe, affordable electricity in 11 of Arizona's 15 counties. Our other active subsidiaries are El Dorado and PNW Power.

Our reportable business segment is our regulated electricity segment, which consists of traditional regulated retail and wholesale electricity businesses (primarily electric service to Native Load customers) and related activities, and includes electricity generation, transmission, and distribution. Our reportable business segment activities are conducted primarily through our wholly-owned subsidiary, APS.
BUSINESS OF ARIZONA PUBLIC SERVICE COMPANY

APS currently provides electric service to approximately 1.4 million customers. We own or lease 6,257 MW of regulated generation capacity, and we hold a mix of both long-term and short-term PPAs for additional capacity. During 2025, no single purchaser or user of energy accounted for more than 1.9% of our electric revenues.
The following map shows APS's retail service territory, including the locations of its generating facilities and principal transmission lines.

To serve its customers, APS obtains power through its various generation stations and through PPAs. Resource planning is an important function necessary to meet Arizona's future energy needs. APS's sources of energy by type used to supply energy to Native Load customers during 2025 were approximately as follows:

APS has a diverse portfolio of existing and planned resources, including biomass, biogas, coal, energy storage, geothermal, natural gas, solar, and wind. APS has an aspirational goal to be carbon-neutral by 2050, meaning that for any GHG emissions still produced by generation resources in 2050, APS will aim to offset these emissions elsewhere. In 2025, the share of APS's energy supply derived from clean resources was approximately 58%, which includes energy from nuclear, renewables, and DSM as well as PPAs with clean resources. Maintaining a balanced and diverse portfolio of resources helps ensure continued reliable service to our customers in the most affordable manner possible. Every three years, APS performs an IRP, a comprehensive study to identify what resources will be necessary to safely, reliably, and affordably meet the demand and energy needs of its customers over the next 15 years. The latest IRP was released in 2023 and APS is currently developing its next IRP due to be filed with the ACC in August 2026. To help ensure competitive costs for resources, APS regularly issues competitive bid solicitations through the ASRFP process, with the most recent ASRFP being issued in 2025. These ASRFPs are open to bids for all resource types, including customer-scale (behind the meter) and utility-scale (in front of the meter) resources.
As energy demand in Arizona continues to grow, APS remains committed to delivering reliable and affordable service to its customers, with a goal of achieving top quartile reliability compared to its

peers. Among other strategies, APS intends to achieve this goal through various methods such as relying on Palo Verde, one of the nation's largest producers of carbon-free energy; seeking a balanced energy mix; managing demand with a modern interactive grid; promoting customer technology and energy efficiency; and optimizing regional resources.

APS also intends to harden its infrastructure in order to improve resiliency, which involves system and operational improvements aimed at reducing the impact of extreme weather events and other disruptions upon APS's operations. Wildfire safety remains a critical focus for APS and other utilities. APS has increased investment in fire mitigation efforts to clear defensible space around its infrastructure, continue ongoing system upgrades, build partnerships with government entities and first responders, and educate customers and communities. Among other resiliency strategies, APS anticipates increasing investments in a modern and more flexible electricity grid with advanced distribution technologies.

APS has ownership interests in or leases the nuclear, gas, oil, coal, and solar generating facilities as well as energy storage facilities described below. For additional information regarding these facilities, see Item 2.

Palo Verde Generating Station — Palo Verde is a 3-unit nuclear power plant located approximately 50 miles west of Phoenix, Arizona. APS operates the plant and owns 29.1% of Palo Verde Units 1 and 3 and approximately 23.9% of Unit 2. In addition, APS leases approximately 5.2% of Unit 2, resulting in a 29.1% combined ownership and leasehold interest in that unit. APS has a total entitlement from Palo Verde of 1,146 MW.

Palo Verde Leases — In 1986, APS entered into agreements with three separate lessor trust entities in order to sell and lease back approximately 42% of its share of Palo Verde Unit 2 and certain common facilities. In 2025, APS purchased two of the three leased interests. The remaining lease for approximately 5.2% of Unit 2 expires in 2033. At the end of the lease renewal period, APS will have the option to purchase the leased assets at their fair market value, extend the lease for up to two years, or return the assets to the lessor. See Note 12 for additional information regarding the Palo Verde Unit 2 sale leaseback transactions.

headings: Our financial condition depends upon APS's ability to recover costs in a timely manner from customers through regulated rates and otherwise execute its business strategy.
The operation of APS's nuclear power plant exposes it to substantial regulatory oversight and potentially significant liabilities and capital expenditures.

APS is subject to numerous environmental laws and regulations, and changes in, or liabilities under, existing or new laws or regulations may increase APS's cost of operations or impact its business plans.

APS faces potential financial risks resulting from climate change litigation and legislative and regulatory efforts to limit GHG emissions, as well as physical and operational risks related to climate effects.

Deregulation or restructuring of the electric industry and other factors may result in increased competition, which could have a significant adverse impact on APS's business and its results of operations.
APS's results of operations can be adversely affected by various factors impacting demand for electricity.
The impact of wildfires could negatively affect APS's results of operations.

The operation of power generation facilities and transmission systems involves risks that could result in reduced output or unscheduled outages or could otherwise significantly impact APS's results of operations.
The lack of access to sufficient supplies of water could have a material adverse impact on APS's business and results of operations.
We are subject to risk related to cybersecurity, IT systems, and unauthorized access to our systems that could adversely affect our business and financial condition.
Changes in technology could create challenges for APS's existing business.
We are subject to employee workforce factors that could adversely affect our business and financial condition.
A downgrade of our credit ratings could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
Our cash flow depends on the performance of APS and its ability to make distributions.
We may not have adequate insurance coverage for liabilities.

Pinnacle West's ability to meet its debt service obligations could be adversely affected because its debt securities are structurally subordinated to the debt securities and other obligations of its subsidiaries.
The use of derivative contracts in the normal course of our business could result in financial losses that negatively impact our results of operations.
Proposals to change policy in Arizona or other states made through ballot initiatives or referenda may increase the Company's cost of operations or impact its business plans.
General economic conditions could materially affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
The market price of our common stock may be volatile.
Certain provisions of our articles of incorporation and bylaws and of Arizona law make it difficult for shareholders to change the composition of our board and may discourage takeover attempts.
paragraphs: In addition to the factors affecting specific business operations identified in the description of these operations contained elsewhere in this report, set forth below are risks and uncertainties that could affect our financial results. Unless otherwise indicated or the context otherwise requires, the following risks and uncertainties apply to Pinnacle West and its subsidiaries, including APS.

APS is subject to comprehensive regulation by several federal, state and local regulatory agencies that significantly influence its business, liquidity and results of operations and its ability to fully recover costs from utility customers in a timely manner. The ACC regulates APS's retail electric rates and FERC regulates rates for wholesale power sales and transmission services. The profitability of APS is affected by the rates it may charge and the timeliness of recovering costs incurred through its rates and adjustor recovery mechanisms. Consequently, our financial condition and results of operations are dependent upon the satisfactory resolution of any APS rate proceedings, adjustor recovery and ancillary matters which may come before the ACC and FERC, including in some cases how court challenges to these regulatory decisions are resolved. Arizona, like certain other states, has a statute that allows the ACC to reopen prior decisions and modify otherwise final orders under certain circumstances. Additionally, given that APS is subject to oversight by several regulatory agencies, a resolution by one may not foreclose potential actions by others for similar or related matters. See Note 14.

The ACC must also approve APS's issuance of equity and debt securities and any significant transfer or encumbrance of APS property used to provide retail electric service and must approve or receive prior notification of certain transactions between us, APS, and our respective affiliates, including the infusion of equity into APS. Decisions made by the ACC or FERC could have a material adverse impact on our financial condition, results of operations, or cash flows.

APS's ability to conduct its business operations and avoid negative operational and financial impacts depends in part upon compliance with federal, state and local laws, judicial decisions, statutes, regulations and ACC requirements, which may be revised from time to time by legislative or other action, and obtaining and maintaining certain regulatory permits, approvals, and certificates.

APS must comply in good faith with all applicable statutes, regulations, rules, tariffs, executive orders and orders of agencies that regulate APS's business, including FERC, NRC, EPA, the ACC, and state and local governmental agencies. These laws, regulations, and agencies regulate many aspects of APS's utility operations, including safety and performance, emissions, siting and construction of facilities, labor and employment, customer service and the rates that APS can charge retail and wholesale customers. Failure to comply can subject APS to, among other things, fines and penalties. For example, under the Energy Policy Act of 2005, FERC can impose penalties (approximately $1.2 million per day per violation) for failure to comply with mandatory electric reliability standards. APS is also required to have numerous permits, approvals and certificates from these agencies. APS believes the necessary permits, approvals and certificates have been obtained for its existing operations and that APS's business is conducted in accordance with applicable laws in all material respects.

Changes in laws or regulations that govern APS, new interpretations of laws and regulations, or the imposition of new or revised laws or regulations could have an adverse impact on the manner in which we operate our business and our results of operations. In particular, new or revised laws or interpretations of existing laws or regulations may impact or call into question the ACC's permissive regulatory authority, which may result in uncertainty as to jurisdictional authority within our state, and uncertainty as to whether ACC decisions will be binding or challenged by other agencies or bodies asserting jurisdiction. We are unable to predict the impact on our business and operating results from any pending or future regulatory or legislative rulemaking.

paragraphs: The following discussion should be read in conjunction with Pinnacle West's Consolidated Financial Statements and APS's Consolidated Financial Statements and the related Notes that appear in Item 8 of this report. This discussion provides a comparison of the 2025 results with 2024 results. For the discussion of 2024 compared to 2023, see Part II. Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations of Pinnacle West Capital Corporation's Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024, which specific discussion is incorporated herein by reference. For information on factors that may cause our actual future results to differ from those we currently seek or anticipate, see "Forward-Looking Statements" at the front of this report and "Risk Factors" in Item 1A.

Pinnacle West is an investor-owned electric utility holding company based in Phoenix, Arizona with consolidated assets of approximately $30 billion. We derive essentially all of our revenues and earnings from our principal subsidiary, APS. Since 1886, APS and its affiliates have provided energy and energy-related products to people and businesses throughout Arizona. APS is Arizona's largest and longest-serving electric company and generates safe, affordable and reliable electricity for approximately 1.4 million retail customers in 11 of Arizona's 15 counties. APS is also the operator and co-owner of Palo Verde — a primary source of electricity for the southwestern United States. Our other active subsidiaries are El Dorado and PNW Power.

Our vision is to create a sustainable energy future for Arizona. Our mission is to serve customers with safe, reliable, and affordable energy. We are committed to delivering operational excellence at the lowest cost possible while aspiring to lower carbon emissions over time.

As energy demand in Arizona continues to grow, we remain committed to delivering reliable service to our customers. We have a goal of achieving top quartile reliability as compared to peers. Key elements to delivering reliable service include resource and transmission planning to secure resource adequacy, planning and procuring resources to ensure sufficient reserve margins, distribution automation and resiliency investments, predictive and preventative maintenance programs, seasonal readiness programs, emergency preparedness, and securing a reliable supply chain. Securing a reliable grid requires ongoing infrastructure investments in addition to investments to support new customer growth.

Balanced Energy Mix. APS strives to procure a balanced energy mix, and we believe this provides the greatest reliability at the lowest cost possible while increasing resiliency. We achieve reliability, in part, through a blend of dispatchable resources, such as natural gas and battery storage, that can provide energy when intermittent resources, such as wind and solar, are unavailable. APS regularly
evaluates the best mix of resources based on a changing operating environment, including changes in generation technology, economics, and policy impacts.

Additional natural gas capacity is necessary to support reliable service and meet increasing energy needs. However, existing natural gas pipelines into Arizona are currently 100% committed. As a result, in July 2025, APS executed a gas transportation precedent agreement to secure a long-term supply of natural gas. The new pipeline is expected to be operational by late 2029 and will be owned and operated by a third-party. See Note 14 for more information. APS also plans to add up to 2,000 MW of flexible natural gas generation to its portfolio, designed to help meet the growing around-the-clock energy needs in Arizona. This generation is expected to serve existing customers and business-as-usual growth through our competitive ASRFP process as well as a new subscription model for large load customers, like data centers and large manufacturers. This subscription model is a commercial construct designed to ensure growth pays for growth while protecting affordability for other customers.

Palo Verde, one of the nation's largest carbon-free energy resources, serves as a foundational part of APS's resource portfolio. The plant is a critical asset to the Southwest, generating more than 32 million MWh – enough power for roughly 3.4 million households, or approximately 8.5 million people. Its continued operation is important to a carbon-neutral future for Arizona and the region, as a reliable, continuous, affordable resource and as a large contributor to the local economy. APS owns or leases 29.1% of Units 1, 2, and 3 Palo Verde. In June 2025, APS entered into agreements to purchase two of the three leased interests in Unit 2. The two subject leased interests represented approximately 7% or 94 MW of Unit 2. The transaction closed in September 2025, leaving one remaining lease for approximately 5.2% of Unit 2 that expires in 2033. See Note 12 for more information. APS's rate case application filed in 2025 (the "2025 Rate Case") includes pro forma adjustments to account for these acquisitions. APS continues to evaluate and pursue options for reliably serving growing customer energy needs and demand.

Wildfire Efforts. Wildfire safety remains a critical focus for APS and other utilities. APS has increased investment in fire mitigation efforts to clear defensible space around its infrastructure, continue ongoing system upgrades, build partnerships with government entities and first responders, and educate customers and communities. APS also increased spend on mitigating the risk associated with trees that could cause hazards, resulting in more of these trees being removed before they could cause outages or wildfires. These programs contribute to customer reliability, responsible forest management and safe communities. With wildfire events in Hawaii, California, and across North America over the last few years, APS has been devoting and intends to continue to devote substantial efforts to analyzing and developing enhancements to its systems and processes to mitigate fire risk within its service territory and communities, including by hardening our infrastructure, deploying new technologies where appropriate, increasing our awareness, implementing operational changes, and enhancing our wildfire response capabilities.

APS uses fire modeling software to identify and calculate risk and target future system improvement investments such as fire-resistant pole wrapping, wood to steel pole conversions, and additional remote-controllable field devices like reclosers and switches. In 2024, APS began installing a system of artificial intelligence-based fire sensing cameras with the ability to detect and alert on fire ignitions. These alerts are sent both to APS and fire response dispatch centers to speed fire response in APS's service territory regardless of the cause of the fire. APS also implemented a public safety power shutoff ("PSPS") program on certain feeders that began in the 2024 fire season, leveraging the additional real-time analysis provided by the modeling software. APS has educated and will continue education outreach to customers and communities that may potentially be impacted by the PSPS program.

APS was selected by DOE's Grid Deployment Office ("GDO") to receive up to $70 million in federal money for fire mitigation and grid infrastructure projects. This funding is part of the GDO's Grid Resilience and Innovation Partnership Program and is contingent on APS negotiating and executing final grant agreements with GDO. Additionally, on May 12, 2025, Arizona Governor Hobbs signed into law a bill that requires Arizona electric utilities to develop and seek approval for wildfire mitigation plans and defines the standard of care with respect to wildfire-related claims by reference to such plans. APS continues to evaluate policy and regulatory options, as well as insurance programs, to mitigate the impact of wildfire events.

We are committed to keeping bills as low as possible for our customers while maintaining high levels of reliability. Inflation has dramatically impacted the cost of goods and services in recent years as shown by the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers ("CPI-U"), which from 2018 through 2024 rose nationally 24.9% and 32.1% in Phoenix. Despite this, APS's average residential rates remained well-below those inflation figures, rising 16.2% for the same period according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration. Inflation has moderated from earlier highs, with CPI-U rising 2.7% nationally and 2.2% in Phoenix over the 12 months ended December 2025. As a result of increased tariffs and supply chain constraints, APS amended several of its agreements from its ASRFP issued in 2023 to mitigate these cost impacts. However, APS remains cautious of potential price increases as a result of current and proposed tariffs, which could lead to higher costs and supply chain constraints, while also monitoring the outcome of the recent U.S. Supreme Court's decision regarding the validity of certain tariffs.

APS's customer affordability initiative includes internal opportunities, such as training and mentoring employees on identifying efficiency opportunities; maintaining inventory to take advantage of lower pricing and avoid expediting fees; entering into long-term contracts to hedge against price volatility, which has allowed APS to mitigate against procurement spend on critical items such as transformers; and implementing automation technologies to enhance efficiencies and increase data-oriented decision making. The customer affordability initiative also includes external opportunities, including a portfolio of customer programs designed to help customers reduce and manage their bills. In the 2025 Rate Case, APS is also seeking to reduce cross-subsidization of customer classes and ensure that growth pays for growth by requesting modifications to its cost allocation methodologies. APS continues to seek opportunities to streamline its business processes, mitigate cost increases, increase employee retention, and improve customer satisfaction.

APS's IRP and competitive ASRFP processes serve important roles in providing reliable and affordable energy to APS's customers. The IRP process helps identify the amount and type of resources required to reliably meet customer needs, while the ASRFP process seeks to meet those needs in a competitive manner based on cost, ability to meet system requirements, and commercial viability.

Pinnacle West 為一間在亞利桑那州鳳凰城設立的投資人所有電力公用事業控股公司，其合併資產約為 30 億美元。我們幾乎所有的營業收入與獲利皆來自主要子公司 APS。自 1886 年起，APS 及其關係企業已為亞利桑那州的個人與企業提供能源與能源相關產品。APS 是亞利桑那州規模最大且服務時間最長的電力公司，並在亞利桑那州 15 個縣中的 11 個縣提供安全且價格合理的電力。我們其他積極營運的子公司為 El Dorado 及 PNW Power。
本公司應報告分部為受規範的電力分部，該分部包含傳統受規範的零售及批發電力業務（主要為原住民負載客戶的電力服務）及相關活動，並包括電力發電、輸電及配電。本公司應報告分部之業務主要透過本公司百分之百出資之子公司 APS 進行。
亞利桑那州公共服務公司業務
APS 目前提供電力服務給約 1.4 萬個客戶。本公司擁有或租賃 6,257 MW 的受規範發電容量，並持有長期及短期 PPAs 的混合組合以取得額外容量。在 2025 年，沒有單一購電者或用電者佔本公司電力收入的 1.9% 以上。
以下地圖顯示 APS 的零售服務範圍，包括其發電設施及主要輸電線路的所在地。
為服務其客戶，APS 透過其各類發電站及 PPAs 取得電力。資源規劃是滿足亞利桑那州未來能源需求的重要功能。在 2025 年，APS 用以供應 Native Load 客戶的能源來源類型約如下：

APS 有包含現有及計畫中的多樣資源組合，包括生物質、沼氣、燃煤、能源儲存、地熱能、天然氣、太陽能及風能。APS 有願景目標於 2050 年實現碳中和，意味著在 2050 年由發電資源產生的任何 GHG 排放，APS 會努力在其他地方抵銷這些排放。在 2025 年，APS 的能源供應來自清潔資源的比例約為 58%，包含核能、再生能源、DSM 以及與清潔資源簽訂的 PPAs。維持一個平衡且多樣的資源組合有助於以最經濟的方式確保持續可靠的服務給客戶。每三年，APS 會進行一次 IRP，這是一項全面研究，以識別未來 15 年內滿足客戶需求及能源需求所需的資源。最新 IRP 於 2023 年發佈，APS 目前正在開發下一次 IRP，預計於 2026 年 8 月提交給 ACC。為確保資源成本具有競爭力，APS 定期透過 ASRFP 流程發出競標邀請，最近一次 ASRFP 於 2025 年發出。這些 ASRFP 開放所有資源類型的競標，包括客戶規模（後端）及電力公司規模（前端）的資源。
隨著亞利桑那州能源需求持續成長，APS 仍致力於為其客戶提供可靠且具成本效益的服務，目標為在同業中達到第一四分位的可靠性。
為達成此目標，APS 計畫透過多種方法，例如倚靠帕洛維德（Palo Verde），這是美國最大的碳中性能源生產者之一；尋求平衡的能源組合；以現代互動電網管理需求；推廣客戶科技與能源效率；以及優化區域資源。

APS 也計畫強化其基礎設施，以提升韌性，這包括系統與運作改善，旨在降低極端天氣事件及其他幹擾對 APS 運作的影響。野火安全仍是 APS 及其他電力公司的重要關注重點。APS 已增加對防火措施的投資，以清理其基礎設施周圍的防禦空間，持續進行系統升級，與政府機構及第一 responders 建立合作關係，並教育客戶與社區。除了其他韌性策略外，APS 預期增加對現代且更具彈性的電力網的投資，並採用先進的配電科技。
APS 擁有或租賃以下所描述的核能、天然氣、石油、煤炭及太陽能發電設施，以及能源儲存設施。有關這些設施的更多資訊，請參閱第 2 項。
帕洛維德發電廠 — 帕洛維德是一座位於亞利桑那州菲尼克斯市西約 50 英里處的 3 個單元核能發電廠。APS 運營該發電廠，並擁有帕洛維德第一及第三單元 29.1% 的權益，以及約 23.9% 的第二單元權益。此外，APS 租賃約 5.2% 的第二單元，使其在該單元的總權益與租賃權益合計為 29.1%。APS 從帕洛維德總共取得 1,146 MW 的發電權。
帕洛維德租賃 — 1986 年，APS 與三個獨立的出租人信託機構簽訂協議，以出售並租回約 42% 的帕洛維德第二單元權益及某些共同設施。2025 年，APS 購買了其中兩個租賃權益。剩餘約 5.2% 的第二單元租賃於 2033 年到期。租賃期滿後，APS 有選擇權可按公平市價購買租賃資產、將租賃期延長最多兩年，或將資產歸還出租人。有關帕洛維德第二單元銷售租賃交易的更多資訊，請參閱附註 12。

paragraphs: 下列討論應配合 Pinnacle West 合併財務資料、APS 合併財務資料以及本報告第 8 項中出現的相關附註一併閱讀。此討論提供 2025 年結果與 2024 年結果的比較。有關 2024 年與 2023 年的比較，請參閱 Pinnacle West Capital Corporation 2024 年 12 月 31 日為結算日之年度報告 Form 10-K 中的第 II 項第 7 節「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析」，該特定討論已於 herein 依引用方式納入。有關可能導致我們實際未來結果與目前預期或追求之結果有所差異的因素，請參閱本報告開頭的「前瞻性陳述」以及第 1A 項「風險因素」。

Pinnacle West 為一家位於亞利桑那州鳳凰城的電力公用事業投資控股公司，其合併資產約為 300 億美元。我們幾乎所有的收入與獲利均來自我們的主要子公司 APS。自 1886 年來，APS 及其關係企業已為亞利桑那州的個人與企業提供能源與能源相關產品。APS 是亞利桑那州規模最大且服務時間最長的電力公司，為亞利桑那州 15 個縣中的 11 個縣約 140 萬零售客戶提供安全、經濟且可靠的電力。APS 也是 Palo Verde 的營運者與共同所有者 —— 這是美國西南部的主要電力來源。我們的其他積極子公司為 El Dorado 與 PNW Power。
我們的願景是為亞利桑那州創造可持續的能源未來。我們的使命是為客戶提供安全、可靠且經濟的能源。我們致力於以最低成本提供優質運營，同時逐步降低碳排放。
隨著亞利桑那州的能源需求持續成長，我們仍致力於為客戶提供可靠的服務。我們的目標是達到與同業相比的前四分位可靠度。提供可靠服務的關鍵要素包括資源與輸電規劃以確保資源充足、規劃與取得資源以確保足夠的備用容量、配電自動化與韌性投資、預測性與預防性維護計畫、季節性準備計畫、應急準備，以及確保可靠的供應鏈。確保可靠的電網需要持續的基礎建設投資，以及支持新客戶成長的投資。
平衡能源組合。APS 勉力取得平衡的能源組合，我們認為這能以最低成本提供最大的可靠度，同時提高韌性。我們的可靠度部分來自於混合使用可調度資源，例如天然氣與電池儲能，這些資源可在風能與太陽能等間歇性資源不可用時提供能源。APS 定期
評估資源組合的最佳組合，根據變動的運營環境，包括發電技術的變化、經濟因素與政策影響。

額外的天然氣容量對於支持可靠的服務與滿足日益增長的能源需求是必要的。然而，現有的天然氣輸送管線進入亞利桑那州目前為 100% 佔用。因此，2025 年 7 月，APS 籤訂了一項天然氣運輸先例協議，以確保長期的天然氣供應。新管線預計於 2029 年年底投入運作，並將由第三方擁有與營運。有關更多資訊，請參閱附註 14。APS 預計將在其組閤中增加最多 2,000 MW 的靈活天然氣發電，以協助滿足亞利桑那州全天候增長的能源需求。此發電將服務現有客戶與業務如常成長，透過我們的競爭性 ASRFP 流程，以及為大型負載客戶（如資料中心與大型製造商）設計的新訂閱模式。此訂閱模式為一種商業結構，旨在確保成長能支應成長，同時保護其他客戶的經濟性。

Palo Verde 是美國最大的碳中性能源資源之一，為 APS 的資源組合提供基礎。該電廠是西南部的重要資產，產生超過 3200 萬兆瓦時的電力 —— 足夠約 340 萬戶家庭，或約 850 萬人使用。其持續運作對亞利桑那州及該地區實現碳中性未來至關重要，作為可靠、持續且經濟的資源，以及對當地經濟的重大貢獻。APS 擁有或租賃 Palo Verde 第 1、2、3 單元的 29.1%。2025 年 6 月，APS 籤訂了購買 Unit 2 兩個租賃權益的協議。這兩個租賃權益代表 Unit 2 約 7% 或 94 MW 的權益。交易於 2025 年 9 月完成，剩餘一個租賃權益約為 Unit 2 的 5.2%，於 2033 年到期。有關更多資訊，請參閱附註 12。APS 在 2025 年提出的電價案（「2025 電價案」）包含這些收購的預計調整。APS 繼續評估並追求可靠服務成長客戶能源需求與需求的選項。

野火應對措施。野火安全仍是APS及其他電力公司的重要關注重點。APS已增加對防火措施的投資，以清理其基礎設施周圍的防禦空間，持續進行系統升級，與政府機構及第一 responders 建立合作關係，並教育客戶與社區。APS亦增加支出以降低可能造成危害的樹木風險，導致更多這些樹木在造成停電或野火之前被移除。這些計畫有助於客戶電力供應的可靠性、負責任的森林管理與安全社區。隨著過去幾年夏威夷、加州及北美地區的野火事件，APS已投入並計畫持續投入大量努力，用以分析並發展其系統與流程的改進，以降低其服務區域與社區的火災風險，包括強化基礎設施、在適當情況下部署新科技、提高警覺性、實施作業變更，以及提升野火應對能力。

APS使用火災模擬軟體來識別並計算風險，並針對未來系統改善投資進行目標設定，例如防火的電桿包覆、木製電桿轉為鋼製電桿，以及額外的遠端可控場端裝置如重合器與開關。2024年，APS開始安裝一套基於人工智慧的火災感測攝影機系統，具備偵測並警示火災點的能力。這些警示會同時傳送至APS與消防應變中心，以加快APS服務區域內的火災應對，無論火災原因為何。APS亦在2024年火災季節開始實施公共安全電力切斷（"PSPS"）計畫，利用模擬軟體提供的額外即時分析功能。APS已教育並會持續教育可能受PSPS計畫影響的客戶與社區。

APS被美國能源部（DOE）的電網部署辦公室（"GDO"）選中，獲取最高達7000萬美元的聯邦資金，用於防火與電網基礎設施專案。此資金為GDO電網韌性與創新合作計畫的一部分，並依賴APS與GDO協商並執行最終的補助協議。此外，2025年5月12日，亞利桑那州州長霍布斯簽署法案，要求亞利桑那州電力公司制定並取得批准野火防範計畫，並以該計畫為準則，界定與野火相關聲請的標準。APS持續評估政策與監管選項，以及保險計畫，以降低野火事件的影響。

我們致力於在維持高水準可靠性的同時，為客戶維持盡可能低的費用。通貨膨脹近年來大幅影響商品與服務的成本，如消費者物價指數（CPI-U）所示，從2018年至2024年，全國物價上漲24.9%，而在鳳凰城則上漲32.1%。儘管如此，APS的平均住宅費用仍遠低於這些通貨膨脹數據，根據美國能源資訊管理局的資料，相同期間內上漲16.2%。通貨膨脹已從較高的水平有所緩和，CPI-U在2025年12月結束的12個月內，全國上漲2.7%，而在鳳凰城則上漲2.2%。由於增加的關稅與供應鏈限制，APS已修改其2023年發出的ASRFP部分協議，以緩解這些成本影響。然而，APS仍對目前及提案中的關稅可能導致的價格上漲保持謹慎，這可能會導致更高的成本與供應鏈限制，同時也監測美國最高法院最近對某些關稅有效性裁決的結果。

APS的客戶負擔能力計畫包括內部機會，例如培訓與指導員工識別效率機會；維持存貨以利用較低價格並避免加急費用；簽訂長期契約以對抗價格波動，這已使APS能降低關鍵項目如變壓器的採購成本；並實施自動化科技以提高效率與增加數據導向的決策。客戶負擔能力計畫亦包括外部機會，包括一套客戶計畫組合，用以協助客戶降低與管理其費用。在2025年費用案中，APS亦計畫減少客戶類別的交叉補貼，並確保成長能支付成長，請求修改其成本分配方法。APS持續尋找機會以簡化其業務流程、緩解成本增加、提高員工留存率，並改善客戶滿意度。
APS的IRP與競爭性ASRFP程序在提供可靠且經濟的能源給APS客戶方面扮演重要角色。IRP程序有助於識別為可靠滿足客戶需求所需的資源數量與類型，而ASRFP程序則以成本、能否滿足系統需求與商業可行性為基礎，以競爭方式滿足這些需求。

headings: 本公司之財務狀況取決於 APS 有能力透過受規範之費率及其它方式及時向客戶回收成本，並執行其業務策略。
APS 運作其核能發電廠，使其面臨重大之監管審查及潛在重大之責任與資本支出。
APS 遵守眾多環境法規，現行或新法規之變更或責任，可能增加 APS 之營運成本或影響其業務計畫。
APS 面臨因氣候變遷訴訟及限制 GHG 排放之立法與監管努力所導致之潛在財務風險，以及與氣候影響相關之實體及營運風險。
電力產業之 deregulation 或重組及其他因素，可能導致競爭增加，進而對 APS 之業務及其營運成果產生重大不利影響。
APS 之營運成果可能受影響於各種影響電力需求之因素。
野火之影響可能對 APS 之營運成果產生負面影響。
電力發電設施及輸電系統之運作涉及風險，可能導致產出減少或非預期停機，或對 APS 之營運成果產生重大影響。
缺乏足夠的水資源可能對 APS 的業務及營運成果產生重大不利影響。
我們面臨與網路安全、資訊系統及未經授權存取我們系統相關的風險，可能對我們的業務及財務狀況產生不利影響。
科技的變更可能對 APS 現有業務造成挑戰。
我們面臨員工人力因素的風險，可能對我們的業務及財務狀況產生不利影響。
我們信用評級的降級可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大且不利的影響。
我們的現金流取決於 APS 及其能否發放分紅的能力。
我們可能無法為相關責任取得足夠的保險保障。
Pinnacle West 未能履行其債務償還義務的風險可能因其債務證券在結構上次於其子公司債務證券及其他義務而受到不利影響。
本公司在正常業務運作中使用衍生合約，可能會導致財務損失，進而對營業收入產生負面影響。
亞利桑那州或其他州透過公投或公民投票提出的政策變更提案，可能會提高本公司的營運成本或影響其業務計畫。
總體經濟狀況可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營業收入產生重大影響。
本公司普通股的市場價格可能出現波動。
本公司章程與章程規則以及亞利桑那州法律的某些條款，使股東難以改變董事會成員組成，並可能阻卻收購嘗試。
paragraphs: 除影響特定業務運作之因素外，本報告其他部分所述之業務運作外，尚有下列可能影響我們財務結果之風險與不確定性。除非另有說明或上下文另有要求，以下風險與不確定性適用於 Pinnacle West 及其子公司，包括 APS。

APS 受多個聯邦、州及地方監管機關之全面監管，這些監管機關對其業務、流動性及營運成果，以及其能否及時從電力用戶處完全回收成本有重大影響。ACC 設定 APS 的零售電力價格，FERC 則規範 wholesale 電力銷售及傳輸服務之價格。APS 的獲利能力受其可收取之價格及透過其價格與調整機制回收成本之時效性所影響。因此，我們之財務狀況與營運成果取決於 ACC 與 FERC 所處理之任何 APS 價格程序、調整機制及相關事項之滿意解決，包括在某些情況下，法院對這些監管決定之挑戰如何解決。亞利桑那州，如同其他一些州一樣，有法律允許 ACC 重新審視先前決定並在特定情況下修改否則已確定之裁決。此外，由於 APS 受多個監管機關監督，一個機關之解決結果可能不會排除其他機關對相似或相關事項採取行動之可能性。請參閱附註 14。
ACC 還必須批准 APS 發行股權與債務證券，以及任何重大轉讓或設定 APS 用以提供零售電力服務之財產，並必須批准或事先通知我們、APS 及我們各自之關係企業之間之某些交易，包括向 APS 注入股權。ACC 或 FERC 之決定可能對我們之財務狀況、營運成果或現金流造成重大不利影響。
APS 進行業務運作並避免負面運營與財務影響之能力，在一定程度上取決於遵守聯邦、州及地方法律、司法判決、法規、ACC 要求，這些可能因立法或其他行動而時常修訂，以及取得並維持某些監管許可、批准與證書。

APS 必須誠實遵守所有適用之法律、法規、規則、運價表、行政命令及監管 APS 之機關之命令，包括 FERC、NRC、EPA、ACC 及州與地方政府機關。這些法律、法規與機關規範 APS 之電力公司運作許多方面，包括安全與表現、排放、設施之設置與建設、勞動與就業、客戶服務及 APS 可對零售與 wholesale 客戶收取之價格。違規可能使 APS 面臨罰款與處罰。例如，根據 2005 年能源政策法案，FERC 可對未遵守強制性電力可靠性標準之行為處以罰款（約每日 120 萬美元）。APS 還必須取得這些機關之多數許可、批准與證書。APS 相信已取得其現有運作所需之許可、批准與證書，且其業務運作符合適用法律之所有重大方面。
影響 APS 之法律或法規之變更、法律或法規之新解釋，或新訂或修訂法律或法規之實施，可能對我們運作業務之方式及營運成果造成不利影響。特別是，新訂或修訂法律或法規之解釋可能影響或質疑 ACC 之監管權限，這可能導致我們州內管轄權之不確定，以及 ACC 之決定是否具有拘束力或是否被其他機關或機構主張管轄權而挑戰之不確定。我們無法預測任何待決或未來監管或立法規則制定對我們業務與營運成果之影響。
